pharm: Centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant; GABA-A and glycinergic activity
quick: 8 mg PO every 12 h (max 16 mg/day), short-term
May take with food to reduce GI upset
Symptom relief; limit duration to 7 days
summary: Thiocolchicoside is a semisynthetic muscle relaxant used short-term for painful muscle spasm. EMA-restricted to 8 mg every 12 hours orally for a maximum of 7 days due to genotoxicity concerns with a metabolite. Contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation. Not FDA-approved.
indications: Adjunctive treatment of painful muscle contractures in acute spinal pathology (short-term)
Painful muscle spasm associated with musculoskeletal and rheumatologic conditions (short-term)

dosage.n: Contraindicated in children/adolescents per EMA restriction

admin: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible duration
Oral: limit to a maximum of 7 days; IM: maximum 5 days
Do not exceed 16 mg/day (oral) or 8 mg/day (IM)
Take with food if gastrointestinal discomfort occurs
Avoid in patients of reproductive potential without contraception due to genotoxicity
moa: A semisynthetic derivative of colchicoside that acts as a centrally acting muscle relaxant. It has agonist activity at GABA-A and glycine (strychnine-sensitive) receptors, producing muscle relaxation and reducing spasticity, with additional anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects on contracted skeletal muscle.

absolute: Women of childbearing potential not using contraception
monitor: Duration of therapy (do not exceed limits)

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. A metabolite is genotoxic (aneugenic) in preclinical studies, raising teratogenic concern. Women of childbearing potential must use effective contraception.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding due to genotoxicity concerns and excretion in milk.
renal: Use with caution; data in renal impairment are limited. Avoid prolonged use.
hepatic: Use with caution; data in hepatic impairment are limited.

moderate: CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedatives) - additive sedation
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce gastrointestinal upset.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive sedation and CNS depression.

monitoring: Limit and document treatment duration (oral 7 days, IM 5 days)
Watch for seizures in predisposed patients
Confirm contraception in women of childbearing potential
counsel: Use only for the prescribed short course; do not extend
Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsy
Do not use if pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy
Report any seizure, rash or breathing difficulty
pk: Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light
pearls: EMA restricted indication and duration due to aneugenic metabolite (genotoxicity)
Strictly short-term: oral maximum 7 days, IM maximum 5 days
Contraindicated in pregnancy, lactation and women without contraception
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless the next dose is near; do not double up. Given the short maximum course, resume the regular twice-daily schedule.
overdose: Overdose may cause sedation, GI disturbance, and seizures in predisposed patients. Treatment is supportive with airway protection, seizure control and monitoring; there is no specific antidote.
